title: The Tuesday Jamie Oliver's Restaurants Closed Their Doors
conflicts: Oliver's personal money is reported as £3m (BBC, Dec 2017), £7.5m plus £5.2m (his FT interview, 2018), £4m more in 2019 (administrators) and about £25m lost in total (The Times, from KPMG's report); each figure is attributed in the story. Creditor losses £83m (The Times, July 2019) vs £80m (Guardian, Jan 2020, KPMG progress report); used 'roughly £80m'. Jobs: up to 1,300 at risk in early reports vs about 1,000 lost on the day; used 1,000.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's 'bootstrapped' to 'mixed': financed by Oliver's holding company and HSBC secured debt, no documented outside equity. Blame limited to Oliver's own words ('I have to take full responsibility'; rents, rates, labour costs) and the 2020 employment tribunal's finding on consultation; the union's criticism and The Times's paraphrase that he was badly advised are left out. NYT interview read via the Irish Times reprint, which converts sums to euros, so no figures taken from it.
